newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Burr-Brown CFO on Q1 revenues.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Burr-Brown CFO on Q1 revenues.

text.p: Burr-Brown Corp chief financial officer Scott Blouin said the company's near-term expectation is for revenues in the first quarter to be flat with the company's fourth quarter revenues of $50.5 million.
He said the company anticipates sequential quarterly revenue growth for the remainder of the year.
For the first quarter ended March 30, 1996, Burr-Brown reported net income of $11.6 million or $0.69 per share on revenues of $61.2 million.
Earlier, Burr-Brown reported fourth quarter net income fell to $0.35 per share or $5.8 million on revenues of $50.5 million from $0.55 a share or $9.4 million on revenues of $69.8 million a year ago.
The maker of electronic components said profitability of its analog and mixed signal business was maintained during the year at the 1995 level of 11 percent despite lower revenue.
Through cost reduction efforts and gains in manufacturing efficiency, the gross margin ratio was improved and sustained at a 50 percent level for the entire year.
It said several of its products have already resulted in volume orders and will begin to contribute significantly to revenue in 1997.
It also said that an increase in order rates observed at the end of the third quarter continued throughout the fourth quarter, resulting in a book-to-bill ratio that exceeded 1.0.
